# Warning: LLM-generated

Tracking PR for kernel fusions and host-dispatch reductions in the eager
metadata section around the captured DeepSeek V4.1 flash-decode forward.
Each item is its own PR (#63393 stacks on #63296; #63523 stacks on #63393;
#63579 stacks on #63523); this branch stacks them so the combined effect
can be A/B tested before the individual PRs are marked ready. Items 6
and 7 are committed directly on this branch.

Fusion scope (from an H200 c16 decode profile, 16 ms ITL):

| # | PR | Change | Launches removed / step |
|---|----|--------|------------------------|
| 1 | #63296 | Fold the SWA validity mask (`torch.ge`) and decode-lens tail fill into the per-group SWA index kernels | 2 x G (16 at G=8) |
| 2 | #63307 | One kernel for `make_dummy`, one for grouped block-table zeroing; cumsum replaced by its closed form | 11 + G (19 at G=8) |
| 3 | #63393 | Batch the G per-group SWA decode index builds into one pointer-indirected launch over a per-step address table | G - 1 (7 at G=8) |
| 4 | #63523 | Host dispatches, not kernels: DP-agreement scalar reads, batch-split host math, and the batched SWA params table move to numpy views and a cached pinned staging table | ~40 dispatches + 1 pinned alloc |
| 5 | #63579 | Split the DFlash buffer padding into one wide launch, build the native indexer decode lens in one kernel, fuse the Gumbel sample finalize | ~120 us eager GPU + ~3 launches |
| 6 | (direct) | One merged `context_wkv_proj` GEMM for all draft layers' context KV, kv_norm folded into the fused KV rope/insert kernel, 2D broadcast entry into draft layer 0 | ~35 us in-graph GPU + 6 launches |
| 7 | (direct) | The dummy path's per-step buffer builds (`make_dummy` init, grouped block-table zero, slot-map pad fill) and the two-range `is_padding` fill stage as rows of the decode prologue parameter table | 3 on tokenless DP ranks + 1 fill |

All five keep buffer addresses and value contracts for downstream
consumers (attention kernels, cudagraph replay, JIT warmup).

The engram hash/lookup pair stays unfused on purpose (a radix sort and a
topk sit between them).

## End-to-end A/B (PD-disaggregated, 2 x 8x H200, all six items)

Common setup: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, prefill and decode on one node each
(8x H200 per node), TP1 x DP8, MTP 3 drafts, NIXL KV transfer
(128Gi CPU tier), 262144 context, llm-d DisaggregatedSet deployment.
aiperf load from semianalysis CC traces (ISL p50 58-84k tokens,
prefix-cache hit 93-96%), 900 s per stage, c8-c128, one run per arm,
identical request sequences in both arms. Same-build repeats on this
cluster give a +-0.5-0.8% throughput and ~+-2% latency-percentile band.
gsm8k (5-shot, chat template, thinking disabled, 1319 samples) ran with
0 errors in every arm.

Campaign dsv41-pd-pr63308-ab-001-20261026-0551: ctl = vllm-main
`00b6c4c5`, exp = main + this branch at `5607ef96`. Both arms build as
native wheels from the same repo through the same build path and run from
the same image digest, so nothing but the fusion commits differs.

aiperf decode (per stage, ctl -> exp):

| stage | ITL p50 | ITL p90 | TTFT p50 | TTFT p90 | output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| c8 | 4.96 -> 4.83 ms (-2.6%) | 5.58 -> 5.37 ms (-3.7%) | 628 -> 622 ms (-1.0%) | 873 -> 847 ms (-3.0%) | 314.5 -> 289.3 |
| c16 | 5.06 -> 4.99 ms (-1.3%) | 5.67 -> 5.49 ms (-3.3%) | 627 -> 631 ms (+0.6%) | 958 -> 974 ms (+1.7%) | 384.6 -> 385.6 |
| c32 | 5.80 -> 5.70 ms (-1.8%) | 6.57 -> 6.42 ms (-2.4%) | 638 -> 641 ms (+0.5%) | 1096 -> 1151 ms (+5.0%) | 1306.0 -> 1308.7 |
| c64 | 6.77 -> 6.66 ms (-1.6%) | 7.86 -> 7.76 ms (-1.4%) | 712 -> 693 ms (-2.7%) | 1318 -> 1311 ms (-0.5%) | 2180.5 -> 2181.9 |
| c128 | 8.88 -> 8.67 ms (-2.4%) | 10.62 -> 10.39 ms (-2.1%) | 884 -> 881 ms (-0.3%) | 1565 -> 1590 ms (+1.6%) | 3843.9 -> 3868.0 |

nyann (ISL/OSL 2048) alongside, TPOT p50: 15.61 -> 15.32,
18.16 -> 17.96, 23.03 -> 22.74 ms; p90 the same shape
(15.72 -> 15.44, 18.31 -> 18.07, 23.11 -> 22.83). 0 errors, no failed
requests in either arm.

gsm8k flexible-extract exact_match 0.9719 +-0.0045 -> 0.9682 +-0.0048,
strict-match 0.9704 +-0.0047 -> 0.9666 +-0.0049 (within stderr); 1319
samples, 0 errors.

Findings:

- Decode latency falls at every measured concurrency in both harnesses:
  aiperf ITL p50 down 1.3-2.6% and p90 down 1.4-3.7% across c8-c128,
  nyann TPOT p50/p90 down 1.1-1.9% across c8-c32. Sixteen of sixteen
  latency measurements move the same way.
- Output throughput holds within +-0.6% at c16-c128. At c8 the CC-trace
  replay sustains an effective concurrency near 2 and same-build
  campaigns on this cluster swing c8 throughput by ~4-8% between runs
  (earlier same-stack arms read 288.9-300.8 tok/s where this ctl read
  314.5), so the c8 throughput gap reads as replay noise; the c8 ITL
  percentiles favor the fusions.
- TTFT p50/p90 moved within the run-to-run spread at every stage.
- gsm8k matches within stderr on both extractors; the accuracy gate for
  the fused kv_norm in item 6 passes.
- No engine restarts in either arm.

## Profiled A/B at c16 (same commits as the e2e run)

Campaign dsv41-pd-pr63308-prof-001-20261026-1326. Same deployment and the
same commits as the e2e A/B (ctl = vllm-main `00b6c4c5`, exp = `5607ef96`),
with the multinode torch profiler (fork of #52595) held identical in both
arms: CPU + CUDA activities, record_shapes, 16-step window on the decode
role, all 8 DP ranks collected. aiperf c16 replay, 180 s per arm, 0 failed
requests (162 and 165 completed).

Client side (ctl -> exp):

| metric | c16 |
|---|---|
| ITL p50 | 5.071 -> 4.873 ms (-3.9%) |
| ITL p90 | 5.745 -> 5.514 ms (-4.0%) |
| TTFT p50 | 656.6 -> 658.6 ms |
| output tok/s | 330.9 -> 334.6 (+1.1%) |

TTFT p90 read 850 -> 903 ms; the 180 s window holds ~20 TTFT samples, so
that tail is noise (the 900 s e2e stages measured c16 TTFT p90 at
958 -> 974 ms).

Trace side, totals over 8 ranks x 16 decode steps:

- Eager `cudaLaunchKernel` calls: 5785 -> 1620 (-72%).
- SWA validity compare (`torch.ge`): 1423 -> 0.
- Per-group SWA index builds: 1024 -> 0, replaced by 128 batched
  launches (G=8 to 1).
- Cumsum / arange / add / scalar-fill family (7 kernel names, 48 calls
  each in ctl): -> 0.
- Gumbel sample finalize chain (399 reduce + 399 scatter-gather + 256
  elementwise): -> 0, replaced by one kernel, 396 calls.
- Integer fills: 2816 -> 1152.
- DFlash input prepare: 17.2 -> 2.2 ms of GPU time per capture (the
  buffer padding moved to one fixed-256-wide launch, 132 calls, 0.19 ms).
- kv_norm RMSNorm launches: 793 -> 392; the norm is folded into the KV
  rope/insert kernel, which is replaced 1:1 (5519 -> 5516 calls, GPU time
  unchanged at 16.6 ms).
- Draft context projection: per-layer [5120, 1792] GEMMs 5918 -> 5516
  calls, replaced by one merged [5120, 1536] GEMM, 132 calls.
- GPU time of the fused-away kernels: ~5.4 ms fully removed plus the
  fill and rms-norm reductions above, replaced by ~1.2 ms of new kernels.

Compute path check: every per-layer kernel holds its call count (5519 vs
5516); NCCL kernels move +3% at flat call counts, which is inter-rank
skew absorbed as collective wait. The two capture windows differ in
decode-batch mode mix, so total in-graph GPU time is not comparable
across arms; the family-by-family counts above are the controlled
comparison.

The ITL gain exceeds the raw GPU-kernel saving because each removed
eager op also costs ~20-40 us of host dispatch per launch; the eager
launch count is the quantity that maps to ITL below saturation.

## Post-campaign refinements

After the first four-PR e2e runs, a code review of the head turned up
four refinements, each landed on the sub-PR that owns the code and
merged into this branch:

- The SWA index kernels' invalid-path `-1` row-clear now stops at
  `num_valid_tokens` (#63296): the pre-fusion kernel never wrote index
  rows past it, and on decode+chunked-prefill steps the far tail spans
  the chunk's rows, where the full-width clears cost megabytes of dead
  stores per step. The lens zero still covers the full buffer tail.
- The batched SWA flush takes the direct per-group path at a single
  group (#63393): at G=1 the table upload fuses nothing. The batched
  kernel also bounds its row-clear the same way and reads its parameter
  table through `_load_ptr`, restoring the 16-byte vectorization hint.
- The params-table H2D copy runs on change, not per step (#63523):
  every row holds addresses and strides of persistent per-group buffers,
  so the table only differs on reallocation or a group-count change; a
  numpy compare guards the copy and event record.
- The native indexer decode-lens kernel (#63579) moved from one program
  per token to a 256-wide block-strided grid, removing the scalar div/mod
  per CTA.

None of these change output values or buffer contracts; the e2e A/B and
the profiled A/B above both measured the refined build.

The same traces ruled out the other candidates from the kernel-duration
list: the 301 us/step `nvjet` GEMM is the in-graph lm_head streaming
~1.85 GB of bf16 weights at tiny M (weight-bandwidth-bound, an lm_head
dtype change, not a fusion); the engram hash/lookup chain is in-graph
with per-layer embedding tables prefetched on a side stream, so batching
the lookups would serialize work the prefetch currently overlaps; the
two paged-MQA metadata builds cannot merge without breaking CUDA-graph
address stability (deep_gemm returns fresh tensors and the DtoD copies
pin them); and folding the image-sentinel mask polarity saves no
launches because both polarities are consumed.

## Draft-prologue fusions (direct)

The draft graph's FULL-cudagraph prologue spent ~105 us of in-graph GPU
per decode step before the draft layers. Commit `e685707e` cuts ~35 us
of it with three fusions:

- The context-KV precompute ran one `fused_wqa_wkv` GEMM
  ([T,5120]x[5120,1792]) per draft layer and discarded the q_lora half
  of each output. A merged `context_wkv_proj` ([T,5120]x[5120,1536])
  projects all layers' WKV in one GEMM; weight loading duplicates each
  `mtp.{i}.attn.wkv` shard into the merged projection, mirroring the
  DeepSeek V4 dspark implementation that already ships this pattern.
  The 512-wide output sections keep the fp8 block-quant shards
  128-aligned, so quantization is unchanged.
- The per-layer kv_norm RMSNorm now runs inside
  `fused_deepseek_v4_kv_rope_insert`, which takes the norm weight and a
  row-strided KV view so the projection output slice is quantized and
  inserted into the cache directly (V4 still norms outside its dummy-q
  insert). The kernel matches the reference RMSNorm to fp8-code
  granularity; a kernel test covers the reduction-order tolerance.
- Draft layer 0 enters with the 2D embedding through the
  `hc_attn_fn_broadcast` path instead of materializing the [24,20480]
  repeat of the entry hidden states.

The e2e A/B includes this item, and gsm8k, the accuracy gate for the
fused kv_norm, matched within stderr. The expected e2e effect (~35 us on
a 5-10 ms ITL) sits under the +-2% same-build repeat band, so it reports
inside the aggregate; the kernel-level prologue timing from the trace
window is the primary evidence for this item.

## Dummy-path prologue fusion (direct)

Commit `8e0be20c` stages the dummy path's per-step buffer builds into
the decode prologue parameter table as three new kinds (`FILL_I64`,
`ZERO_ROWS`, `DUMMY_BATCH`):

- A DP rank with no tokens still builds a dummy batch every step: the
  `make_dummy` init kernel, the grouped block-table row zeroing, and
  the slot-mapping pad fill each launch separately. They now retire as
  rows of one prologue launch; with the attention phases' megakernel
  that is 4 launches down to 2 on tokenless steps.
- The dummy rows write the shared step buffers (`seq_lens`,
  `query_start_loc`, `positions`) that the attention-phase prologue
  rows read, and one launch gives no inter-CTA ordering, so the early
  bracket never shares a launch with the attention bracket: it flushes
  at the top of `prepare_attn`, before the replay warmup and slot
  padding read those buffers. Paths that populate zeroed rows or run
  outside a single plain decode step (state slots, dummy context, PCP,
  DCP, multi-ubatch, randomized inputs) keep the direct launches.
- The two-range `is_padding` fill in the sample path becomes one
  `_fill_is_padding_kernel` launch.

Buffer contracts hold: staged buffers are byte-identical to the direct
launches, block-table zeroing still clears dirty rows past `num_reqs`,
and the persistent-tensor addresses the CUDA graph capture relies on
are unchanged. CUDA-gated tests in
`tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_dummy_prologue.py` compare staged vs direct
buffer contents; ruff and CPU import checks pass locally, and the GPU
tests are pending a CI run. This item is not yet covered by an e2e A/B
arm.

## Compressed-slot padding-gap fix (direct)

Commit `0b86f03d8` fixes a correctness bug that `550e44226f`
introduced when it moved the compressed slot mapping's `out.fill_(-1)`
into the kernel: the in-kernel tail clear started at the padded
`num_tokens`, but full-CUDA-graph decode keeps `query_start_loc` flat
below the padded token count, so the gap `[qsl[num_rows], num_tokens)`
held the previous step's slot ids. The captured indexer K store
replays over the full padded width and writes through every
non-negative slot, so stale ids in that gap corrupted the indexer K
cache of live requests: the 2026-10-28 e2e run decoded garbage from
the first traffic step (speculative acceptance 0.000, gsm8k
generations running to the length cap, and the run ended in the
`indexSelectSmallIndex` assert after NaN logits).

The tail now reads its start from `qsl[num_rows]` — where the request
programs stop — on device; the host cannot know that value without a
sync, so both launch sites size the tail grid for the widest tail. The
`num_tokens` kernel argument is gone with it, and the draft rebuild is
unchanged (its arange qsl already ends at `num_rows`). A CUDA-gated
regression test seeds a stale `out` buffer and checks the flat-padded
gap clears to PAD.

## CuTe DSL port of the KV rope/insert kernel (direct)

Commit `cad2bcb10` replaces the
`fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert` CUDA C source and its four
registered ops with a CuTe DSL module that exposes the same entry
points under the same positional schemas (follow-ups `993a6fcbb`,
`9f3956550d`). The math carries over with fp32 accumulation, the KV
branch's bf16 double-round before the absmax, the warp shuffle
reduction order, and the exponent-field UE8M0 scales, over both paged
record layouts (V4 584 B/token, V4.1 mxfp8 528 B/token) and the
full-cache bf16/fp8 variants. The six production call sites import the
module at function scope under a `has_cutedsl()` gate and fail closed
with a named RuntimeError when the DSL package is absent. Known gap:
the `.cu` also built for ROCm, so AMD paths that reached these ops now
refuse instead of running; restoring an AMD implementation is follow-up
work.

The e2e rerun after the slot-tail fix above still decoded garbage
(gsm8k exact_match 0.0000), so the kernel went through a value-level
differential against the reference on an H200 pod. The port had four
defects, each invisible to a clean launch because it corrupts values
while running at full speed, and each caught only by the port's own
suite, which had never been executed (216 of 227 tests failed).
`798a6c99f` fixes them:

- `bf16x2_to_fp32x2` returns the low half first. The port unpacked it
  as (high, low) in `_decode_words` and `_apply_kv_norm`, so every bf16
  pair was loaded with its two elements swapped: Q, KV V4 records,
  mxfp8, combined, and both full-cache variants wrote pairwise-swapped
  values.
- The paged kernel's V4-record RoPE store took its per-lane word offset
  as `(dim_base - NOPE_DIM) // 4`. That difference is an element count
  and a uint32 word holds two bf16s, so consecutive rope lanes wrote
  overlapping word ranges (a write race) and the last 12 words of every
  record stayed unwritten. The stride is now `// 2`.
- The bf16 wrapper's unused `q_fp8` stand-in carried a zero head count
  against the head dim the JIT binds across one call's arguments. The
  stand-in now takes the real head count.
- Q-less full-cache launches compiled their warmup fakes with
  `num_heads_q == 0`, and a zero shape mode is not a legal CuTe layout.
  The warmup fake floors the head count at one. The grid never
  dispatches a Q slot when `num_heads_q == 0`, so the stand-in is never
  read.

The rope region now compares with a one-bf16-ULP slack
(`rtol=1e-2, atol=1e-6`, previously ROCm-only): the DSL contracts the
rotation's two fp32 products into an FMA, as nvcc did for the CUDA
original, while torch's reference rounds each product separately.

`0c1bcad95` repairs three test fixtures that predate or overshoot the
fusions. The dspark compressor fixture stubbed `attn` without the
`kv_norm` attributes `_insert_context_kv` has read since the prologue
fusion, so all 32 parametrizations died on the fixture before reaching
any kernel; its oracle now drives the kv-only op with the same norm
arguments, keeping the comparison byte-exact over the glue the dspark
path owns (attribute reads, scale, flags, strided cache binding, graph
replay) while the norm math stays covered by the kernel suite. The
batched decode-indices test poisoned index rows across the whole token
range, past the decode boundary the decode-phase launch clears. The
dummy-prologue test built its scratch with `torch.full(6, ...)`,
passing 6 as the fill value where the shape is a tuple.

The suites pass on an H200 pod in the wheel-build environment: 227
port, 136 compressor, 55 indexer, 3 prologue, 36 swa-visible tests.
The 26 nvfp4 compressor parametrizations that fail there are ptxas
sm_90a environment failures in the image, on a quant path this branch
does not exercise. The e2e rerun with the port fixes is running.

## Cooperative candidate selection on the stock decode path (direct)

Commit `9e2df243a` routes the stock decode branch's candidate-block
selection through `cooperative_topk`. The c16 decode trace showed the
selection spending ~82 us of stream time per step in the `torch.topk`
fallback, nineteen mbtopk and cub launches plus the trailing
`radixSortKVInPlace` of the sorted=True sort, while the main token
top-k on the same step already ran the single-wave `cooperative_topk`
kernel. `select_candidate_blocks_cooperative` existed for the
specialized decode path only, so stock decode on Hopper took the
fallback unconditionally.

The commit moves the cooperative selection (prefix score kernel,
finalize kernel, shape gate) from
`models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/attention/candidate_topk.py`
into `kernels/attention/dsa/candidate_blocks.py` beside the reference
kernel, deletes the old module, and dispatches from the stock decode
branch when each row carries its own fp32 bounds and
`supports_cooperative_candidates` accepts the shape (at most 64 rows,
k in {512, 1024, 2048}, 16-byte aligned score rows). DeepSelect GPUs,
rows with shared bounds, and every prefill chunk keep the reference
path. Candidate sets match the reference except for fp32 boundary
ties, the contract the specialized path already ships. The specialized
path and its SM100 equivalence tests import from the new location
unchanged.

When the sub-PRs merge, this branch can be fast-forwarded to main and
closed.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

Closing the tracking PR. The combined effect measured above (1.3-2.6% ITL p50 and 1.4-3.7% p90 in the e2e A/B, ~4% at c16 in the profiled window) doesn't justify the complexity of the fused eager-metadata path, so we're dropping the fusion work rather than stacking it further.

@tlrmchlsmth thanks for the review. The CuTe DSL rewrite you asked for is on this branch (cad2bcb10, same entry points and positional schemas); if it's ever useful as a standalone swap for the .cu kernel, the gap to close first is the ROCm build the .cu had.
Can this be rewritten using CuTeDSL? IIUC this kernel is only applicable to DSv4 and I'd like to use jitted kernels in such cases rather than add binary size and compile time

  (earlier same-stack arms read 288.9-300.8 tok/s where this ctl read
  314.5), so the c8 throughput gap reads as replay noise; the c8 ITL
  percentiles favor the fusions.
- TTFT p50/p90 moved within the run-to-run spread at every stage.
- gsm8k matches within stderr on both extractors; the accuracy gate for
  the fused kv_norm in item 6 passes.
- No engine restarts in either arm.

## Profiled A/B at c16 (same commits as the e2e run)

Campaign dsv41-pd-pr63308-prof-001-20261026-1326. Same deployment and the
same commits as the e2e A/B (ctl = vllm-main `00b6c4c5`, exp = `5607ef96`),
with the multinode torch profiler (fork of #52595) held identical in both
arms: CPU + CUDA activities, record_shapes, 16-step window on the decode
role, all 8 DP ranks collected. aiperf c16 replay, 180 s per arm, 0 failed
requests (162 and 165 completed).

Client side (ctl -> exp):

| metric | c16 |
|---|---|
| ITL p50 | 5.071 -> 4.873 ms (-3.9%) |
| ITL p90 | 5.745 -> 5.514 ms (-4.0%) |
| TTFT p50 | 656.6 -> 658.6 ms |
| output tok/s | 330.9 -> 334.6 (+1.1%) |

TTFT p90 read 850 -> 903 ms; the 180 s window holds ~20 TTFT samples, so
that tail is noise (the 900 s e2e stages measured c16 TTFT p90 at
958 -> 974 ms).

Trace side, totals over 8 ranks x 16 decode steps:

- Eager `cudaLaunchKernel` calls: 5785 -> 1620 (-72%).
- SWA validity compare (`torch.ge`): 1423 -> 0.
- Per-group SWA index builds: 1024 -> 0, replaced by 128 batched
  launches (G=8 to 1).
- Cumsum / arange / add / scalar-fill family (7 kernel names, 48 calls
  each in ctl): -> 0.
- Gumbel sample finalize chain (399 reduce + 399 scatter-gather + 256
  elementwise): -> 0, replaced by one kernel, 396 calls.
- Integer fills: 2816 -> 1152.
- DFlash input prepare: 17.2 -> 2.2 ms of GPU time per capture (the
  buffer padding moved to one fixed-256-wide launch, 132 calls, 0.19 ms).
- kv_norm RMSNorm launches: 793 -> 392; the norm is folded into the KV
  rope/insert kernel, which is replaced 1:1 (5519 -> 5516 calls, GPU time
  unchanged at 16.6 ms).
- Draft context projection: per-layer [5120, 1792] GEMMs 5918 -> 5516
  calls, replaced by one merged [5120, 1536] GEMM, 132 calls.
- GPU time of the fused-away kernels: ~5.4 ms fully removed plus the
  fill and rms-norm reductions above, replaced by ~1.2 ms of new kernels.

Compute path check: every per-layer kernel holds its call count (5519 vs
5516); NCCL kernels move +3% at flat call counts, which is inter-rank
skew absorbed as collective wait. The two capture windows differ in
decode-batch mode mix, so total in-graph GPU time is not comparable
across arms; the family-by-family counts above are the controlled
comparison.

The ITL gain exceeds the raw GPU-kernel saving because each removed
eager op also costs ~20-40 us of host dispatch per launch; the eager
launch count is the quantity that maps to ITL below saturation.

## Post-campaign refinements

After the first four-PR e2e runs, a code review of the head turned up
four refinements, each landed on the sub-PR that owns the code and
merged into this branch:

- The SWA index kernels' invalid-path `-1` row-clear now stops at
  `num_valid_tokens` (#63296): the pre-fusion kernel never wrote index
  rows past it, and on decode+chunked-prefill steps the far tail spans
  the chunk's rows, where the full-width clears cost megabytes of dead
  stores per step. The lens zero still covers the full buffer tail.
- The batched SWA flush takes the direct per-group path at a single
  group (#63393): at G=1 the table upload fuses nothing. The batched
  kernel also bounds its row-clear the same way and reads its parameter
  table through `_load_ptr`, restoring the 16-byte vectorization hint.
- The params-table H2D copy runs on change, not per step (#63523):
  every row holds addresses and strides of persistent per-group buffers,
  so the table only differs on reallocation or a group-count change; a
  numpy compare guards the copy and event record.
- The native indexer decode-lens kernel (#63579) moved from one program
  per token to a 256-wide block-strided grid, removing the scalar div/mod
  per CTA.

None of these change output values or buffer contracts; the e2e A/B and
the profiled A/B above both measured the refined build.

The same traces ruled out the other candidates from the kernel-duration
list: the 301 us/step `nvjet` GEMM is the in-graph lm_head streaming
~1.85 GB of bf16 weights at tiny M (weight-bandwidth-bound, an lm_head
dtype change, not a fusion); the engram hash/lookup chain is in-graph
with per-layer embedding tables prefetched on a side stream, so batching
the lookups would serialize work the prefetch currently overlaps; the
two paged-MQA metadata builds cannot merge without breaking CUDA-graph
address stability (deep_gemm returns fresh tensors and the DtoD copies
pin them); and folding the image-sentinel mask polarity saves no
launches because both polarities are consumed.

## Draft-prologue fusions (direct)

The draft graph's FULL-cudagraph prologue spent ~105 us of in-graph GPU
per decode step before the draft layers. Commit `e685707e` cuts ~35 us
of it with three fusions:

- The context-KV precompute ran one `fused_wqa_wkv` GEMM
  ([T,5120]x[5120,1792]) per draft layer and discarded the q_lora half
  of each output. A merged `context_wkv_proj` ([T,5120]x[5120,1536])
  projects all layers' WKV in one GEMM; weight loading duplicates each
  `mtp.{i}.attn.wkv` shard into the merged projection, mirroring the
  DeepSeek V4 dspark implementation that already ships this pattern.
  The 512-wide output sections keep the fp8 block-quant shards
  128-aligned, so quantization is unchanged.
- The per-layer kv_norm RMSNorm now runs inside
  `fused_deepseek_v4_kv_rope_insert`, which takes the norm weight and a
  row-strided KV view so the projection output slice is quantized and
  inserted into the cache directly (V4 still norms outside its dummy-q
  insert). The kernel matches the reference RMSNorm to fp8-code
  granularity; a kernel test covers the reduction-order tolerance.
- Draft layer 0 enters with the 2D embedding through the
  `hc_attn_fn_broadcast` path instead of materializing the [24,20480]
  repeat of the entry hidden states.

The e2e A/B includes this item, and gsm8k, the accuracy gate for the
fused kv_norm, matched within stderr. The expected e2e effect (~35 us on
a 5-10 ms ITL) sits under the +-2% same-build repeat band, so it reports
inside the aggregate; the kernel-level prologue timing from the trace
window is the primary evidence for this item.

## Dummy-path prologue fusion (direct)

Commit `8e0be20c` stages the dummy path's per-step buffer builds into
the decode prologue parameter table as three new kinds (`FILL_I64`,
`ZERO_ROWS`, `DUMMY_BATCH`):

- A DP rank with no tokens still builds a dummy batch every step: the
  `make_dummy` init kernel, the grouped block-table row zeroing, and
  the slot-mapping pad fill each launch separately. They now retire as
  rows of one prologue launch; with the attention phases' megakernel
  that is 4 launches down to 2 on tokenless steps.
- The dummy rows write the shared step buffers (`seq_lens`,
  `query_start_loc`, `positions`) that the attention-phase prologue
  rows read, and one launch gives no inter-CTA ordering, so the early
  bracket never shares a launch with the attention bracket: it flushes
  at the top of `prepare_attn`, before the replay warmup and slot
  padding read those buffers. Paths that populate zeroed rows or run
  outside a single plain decode step (state slots, dummy context, PCP,
  DCP, multi-ubatch, randomized inputs) keep the direct launches.
- The two-range `is_padding` fill in the sample path becomes one
  `_fill_is_padding_kernel` launch.

Buffer contracts hold: staged buffers are byte-identical to the direct
launches, block-table zeroing still clears dirty rows past `num_reqs`,
and the persistent-tensor addresses the CUDA graph capture relies on
are unchanged. CUDA-gated tests in
`tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_dummy_prologue.py` compare staged vs direct
buffer contents; ruff and CPU import checks pass locally, and the GPU
tests are pending a CI run. This item is not yet covered by an e2e A/B
arm.

## Compressed-slot padding-gap fix (direct)

Commit `0b86f03d8` fixes a correctness bug that `550e44226f`
introduced when it moved the compressed slot mapping's `out.fill_(-1)`
into the kernel: the in-kernel tail clear started at the padded
`num_tokens`, but full-CUDA-graph decode keeps `query_start_loc` flat
below the padded token count, so the gap `[qsl[num_rows], num_tokens)`
held the previous step's slot ids. The captured indexer K store
replays over the full padded width and writes through every
non-negative slot, so stale ids in that gap corrupted the indexer K
cache of live requests: the 2026-10-28 e2e run decoded garbage from
the first traffic step (speculative acceptance 0.000, gsm8k
generations running to the length cap, and the run ended in the
`indexSelectSmallIndex` assert after NaN logits).

The tail now reads its start from `qsl[num_rows]` — where the request
programs stop — on device; the host cannot know that value without a
sync, so both launch sites size the tail grid for the widest tail. The
`num_tokens` kernel argument is gone with it, and the draft rebuild is
unchanged (its arange qsl already ends at `num_rows`). A CUDA-gated
regression test seeds a stale `out` buffer and checks the flat-padded
gap clears to PAD.

## CuTe DSL port of the KV rope/insert kernel (direct)

Commit `cad2bcb10` replaces the
`fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert` CUDA C source and its four
registered ops with a CuTe DSL module that exposes the same entry
points under the same positional schemas (follow-ups `993a6fcbb`,
`9f3956550d`). The math carries over with fp32 accumulation, the KV
branch's bf16 double-round before the absmax, the warp shuffle
reduction order, and the exponent-field UE8M0 scales, over both paged
record layouts (V4 584 B/token, V4.1 mxfp8 528 B/token) and the
full-cache bf16/fp8 variants. The six production call sites import the
module at function scope under a `has_cutedsl()` gate and fail closed
with a named RuntimeError when the DSL package is absent. Known gap:
the `.cu` also built for ROCm, so AMD paths that reached these ops now
refuse instead of running; restoring an AMD implementation is follow-up
work.

The e2e rerun after the slot-tail fix above still decoded garbage
(gsm8k exact_match 0.0000), so the kernel went through a value-level
differential against the reference on an H200 pod. The port had four
defects, each invisible to a clean launch because it corrupts values
while running at full speed, and each caught only by the port's own
suite, which had never been executed (216 of 227 tests failed).
`798a6c99f` fixes them:

- `bf16x2_to_fp32x2` returns the low half first. The port unpacked it
  as (high, low) in `_decode_words` and `_apply_kv_norm`, so every bf16
  pair was loaded with its two elements swapped: Q, KV V4 records,
  mxfp8, combined, and both full-cache variants wrote pairwise-swapped
  values.
- The paged kernel's V4-record RoPE store took its per-lane word offset
  as `(dim_base - NOPE_DIM) // 4`. That difference is an element count
  and a uint32 word holds two bf16s, so consecutive rope lanes wrote
  overlapping word ranges (a write race) and the last 12 words of every
  record stayed unwritten. The stride is now `// 2`.
- The bf16 wrapper's unused `q_fp8` stand-in carried a zero head count
  against the head dim the JIT binds across one call's arguments. The
  stand-in now takes the real head count.
- Q-less full-cache launches compiled their warmup fakes with
  `num_heads_q == 0`, and a zero shape mode is not a legal CuTe layout.
  The warmup fake floors the head count at one. The grid never
  dispatches a Q slot when `num_heads_q == 0`, so the stand-in is never
  read.

The rope region now compares with a one-bf16-ULP slack
(`rtol=1e-2, atol=1e-6`, previously ROCm-only): the DSL contracts the
rotation's two fp32 products into an FMA, as nvcc did for the CUDA
original, while torch's reference rounds each product separately.

`0c1bcad95` repairs three test fixtures that predate or overshoot the
fusions. The dspark compressor fixture stubbed `attn` without the
`kv_norm` attributes `_insert_context_kv` has read since the prologue
fusion, so all 32 parametrizations died on the fixture before reaching
any kernel; its oracle now drives the kv-only op with the same norm
arguments, keeping the comparison byte-exact over the glue the dspark
path owns (attribute reads, scale, flags, strided cache binding, graph
replay) while the norm math stays covered by the kernel suite. The
batched decode-indices test poisoned index rows across the whole token
range, past the decode boundary the decode-phase launch clears. The
dummy-prologue test built its scratch with `torch.full(6, ...)`,
passing 6 as the fill value where the shape is a tuple.

The suites pass on an H200 pod in the wheel-build environment: 227
port, 136 compressor, 55 indexer, 3 prologue, 36 swa-visible tests.
The 26 nvfp4 compressor parametrizations that fail there are ptxas
sm_90a environment failures in the image, on a quant path this branch
does not exercise. The e2e rerun with the port fixes is running.

## Cooperative candidate selection on the stock decode path (direct)

Commit `9e2df243a` routes the stock decode branch's candidate-block
selection through `cooperative_topk`. The c16 decode trace showed the
selection spending ~82 us of stream time per step in the `torch.topk`
fallback, nineteen mbtopk and cub launches plus the trailing
`radixSortKVInPlace` of the sorted=True sort, while the main token
top-k on the same step already ran the single-wave `cooperative_topk`
kernel. `select_candidate_blocks_cooperative` existed for the
specialized decode path only, so stock decode on Hopper took the
fallback unconditionally.

The commit moves the cooperative selection (prefix score kernel,
finalize kernel, shape gate) from
`models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/attention/candidate_topk.py`
into `kernels/attention/dsa/candidate_blocks.py` beside the reference
kernel, deletes the old module, and dispatches from the stock decode
branch when each row carries its own fp32 bounds and
`supports_cooperative_candidates` accepts the shape (at most 64 rows,
k in {512, 1024, 2048}, 16-byte aligned score rows). DeepSelect GPUs,
rows with shared bounds, and every prefill chunk keep the reference
path. Candidate sets match the reference except for fp32 boundary
ties, the contract the specialized path already ships. The specialized
path and its SM100 equivalence tests import from the new location
unchanged.

When the sub-PRs merge, this branch can be fast-forwarded to main and
closed.

+"""The dummy path's buffer builds stage into the decode prologue batch.
+
+A DP rank with no tokens still builds a dummy batch every step; its three
+launches (dummy-buffer init, block-table row zeroing, slot-mapping pad fill)
+must produce byte-identical buffers when staged into one prologue launch.

+def snapshot_dummy_buffers(
+    batch: InputBatch, buffers: InputBuffers, num_reqs: int, num_tokens: int
+) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
+    max_num_reqs = buffers.seq_lens.shape[0]
+    return {
+        "idx_mapping": batch.idx_mapping.clone(),
+        "expanded_local_pos": batch.expanded_local_pos.clone(),
+        "cu_num_logits": batch.cu_num_logits.clone(),
+        "logits_indices": batch.logits_indices.clone(),
+        "seq_lens": buffers.seq_lens.clone(),
+        "query_start_loc": buffers.query_start_loc.clone(),
+        "input_ids": buffers.input_ids[:num_tokens].clone(),
+        "positions": buffers.positions[:num_tokens].clone(),
+        "is_padding": buffers.is_padding[:num_tokens].clone(),
+        "seq_lens_tail": buffers.seq_lens[num_reqs:max_num_reqs].clone(),
+        "qsl_tail": buffers.query_start_loc[num_reqs + 1 :].clone(),
+    }
+
+
+def poison_dummy_buffers(buffers: InputBuffers, num_tokens: int) -> None:
+    buffers.seq_lens.fill_(-3)
+    buffers.query_start_loc.fill_(-5)
+    buffers.input_ids[:num_tokens].fill_(77)
+    buffers.positions[:num_tokens].fill_(9)
+    buffers.is_padding[:num_tokens].fill_(True)

+    prologue = DecodePrologueBatch(device)
+    prologue.begin(decode_only=True)

+    # direct fallback path.
+    scratch = torch.full((6,), -11, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)

+"""Fused DeepseekV4-MLA Q-norm/RoPE + KV RoPE/quant/insert, CuTe DSL port.
+
+Replaces csrc/fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert_kernel.cu. One warp owns
+one (token, head_slot) pair, 32 lanes x 16 elements = the 512-wide head:
+
+  slot < num_heads_q                     -> live Q  (optional RMSNorm + RoPE,
+                                             zero-padded to q_head_padded)
+  num_heads_q <= slot < q_head_padded    -> pad Q   (zero fill)
+  slot == q_head_padded                  -> KV      (RoPE + UE8M0 FP8 quant +
+                                             paged-cache insert)
+
+RoPE is GPT-J interleaved-pair on dims [448, 512), all math fp32, cos_sin
+layout [max_pos, 64] = cos || sin. Q output optionally lands in FlashMLA's
+chunk-interleaved layout (32 chunks of [num_heads, 16]).
+
+Paged-cache record layout per block of bs tokens, selected by kv_mxfp8:
+  V4    (584 B/token): [0, bs*576) token data (448 fp8 + 128 bf16 each),
+         then [bs*576, bs*584) UE8M0 scales, 7 real + 1 pad per token.
+  V4.1  (528 B/token, kv_mxfp8): per-token inline records,
+         [i*528, i*528+512) fp8 data + [i*528+512, (i+1)*528) 16 UE8M0
+         scales, one per 32 dims; RoPE dims are quantized too.
+
+The full-cache variants write a contiguous 512-wide token row in the cache's
+own dtype (bf16, or per-tensor-scaled e4m3) with no Q padding.
+
+Bit-exactness notes carried over from the .cu: the KV branch double-rounds
+through bf16 before the absmax, the warp reductions use the same shuffle
+order (fp addition is not associative), and ceil(log2(absmax/448)) is
+computed from the float's exponent field, which is exact for normal inputs.

+        sum_sq = sum_sq + elems[i] * elems[i]

+    fixed byte offsets within a block, so anything else was never a valid
+    input. Returns (data, scale):

+             scale [B, bs, 8] u8 stride (S0, 8, 1)    (tail after bs*576)
+      mxfp8: data [B, bs, 128] u32 stride (S0//4, 132, 1),
+             scale [B, bs, 16] u8 stride (S0, 528, 1) (inline per token)

+    if k_cache.dim() == 2:
+        flat = k_cache
+        if flat.stride(1) != 1:
+            raise ValueError("k_cache rows must be byte-contiguous (stride 1)")
+    elif k_cache.dim() == 3:
+        if k_cache.stride(2) != 1:
+            raise ValueError("k_cache rows must be byte-contiguous (stride 1)")
+        if k_cache.stride(1) != k_cache.shape[2]:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "k_cache rows must be packed (stride(1) == size(2)); the "
+                "record layout is addressed at fixed offsets within a block"
+            )
+        flat = k_cache.view(k_cache.shape[0], -1)
+    else:
+        raise ValueError(f"k_cache must be 2D or 3D, got {k_cache.dim()}D")
+    if flat.shape[1] < block_bytes:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"k_cache row width {flat.shape[1]} is smaller than one "
+            f"{cache_block_size}-token block ({block_bytes} bytes)"

+        raise ValueError("k_cache block stride must be 4-byte aligned")

+) -> None:
+    if not current_platform.is_cuda():
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"{op_name}: the CuTe DSL port is CUDA-only; this platform has "
+            "no implementation"
+        )
+    if not kv.is_cuda:
+        raise ValueError(f"{op_name}: kv must be a CUDA tensor")
+    if kv.dtype == torch.float16:
+        raise NotImplementedError(
+            f"{op_name}: float16 is not ported to the CuTe DSL kernel"
+        )
+    if kv.dtype != torch.bfloat16:
+        raise ValueError(f"{op_name}: kv must be bfloat16, got {kv.dtype}")
+    if kv.dim() != 2 or kv.shape[1] != HEAD_DIM or kv.stride(1) != 1:
+        raise ValueError(f"{op_name}: kv must be [tokens, {HEAD_DIM}] row-major")
+    if kv.stride(0) % 2 != 0:
+        raise ValueError(f"{op_name}: kv row stride must be even")
+    for name, tensor in (
+        ("slot_mapping", slot_mapping),
+        ("position_ids", position_ids),
+    ):
+        if (
+            tensor.dtype != torch.int64
+            or tensor.dim() != 1
+            or not tensor.is_contiguous()
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(f"{op_name}: {name} must be contiguous 1D int64")
+        if tensor.device != kv.device:
+            raise ValueError(f"{op_name}: {name} must be on the KV device")
+    if position_ids.shape[0] != kv.shape[0]:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{op_name}: positions must match KV rows "
+            f"({position_ids.shape[0]} vs {kv.shape[0]})"
+        )
+    if slot_mapping.shape[0] > kv.shape[0]:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{op_name}: slot_mapping must not exceed KV rows "
+            f"({slot_mapping.shape[0]} vs {kv.shape[0]})"
+        )
+    if (
+        cos_sin_cache.dtype != torch.float32
+        or cos_sin_cache.dim() != 2
+        or cos_sin_cache.shape[1] != ROPE_DIM
+        or not cos_sin_cache.is_contiguous()
+    ):
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{op_name}: cos_sin_cache must be contiguous float32 "
+            f"[max_pos, {ROPE_DIM}]"
+        )
+    if cos_sin_cache.device != kv.device:
+        raise ValueError(f"{op_name}: cos_sin_cache must be on the KV device")

+
+def _check_scalar(
+    op_name: str, name: str, scale: torch.Tensor, device: torch.device
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    if scale.dtype != torch.float32 or scale.numel() != 1:
+        raise ValueError(f"{op_name}: {name} must be one float32 scalar")
+    if scale.device != device:
+        raise ValueError(f"{op_name}: {name} must be on the KV device")
+    return scale.reshape(1)

+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class PagedCompileKey:
+    num_heads_q: int
+    q_head_padded: int
+    apply_q_norm: bool
+    apply_q_rope: bool
+    is_q_interleaved: bool
+    kv_mxfp8: bool
+    has_kv_norm: bool
+    reduced_grid: bool
+    eps: float

+class _PagedInsertKernel(VllmCuTeDSLJitKernel[PagedCompileKey]):
+    """Paged-record variant: V4/V4.1 UE8M0 quantizing insert."""
+
+    CompileKey = PagedCompileKey
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def kernel(compile_key: PagedCompileKey) -> Any:
+        HQ = compile_key.num_heads_q
+        QP = compile_key.q_head_padded
+        APPLY_Q_NORM = compile_key.apply_q_norm
+        APPLY_Q_ROPE = compile_key.apply_q_rope
+        Q_INTERLEAVED = compile_key.is_q_interleaved
+        KV_MXFP8 = compile_key.kv_mxfp8
+        HAS_KV_NORM = compile_key.has_kv_norm
+        REDUCED = compile_key.reduced_grid
+        EPS = Float32(compile_key.eps)
+        USE_PDL = current_platform.is_arch_support_pdl()
+
+        def q_in_off(token: Int32, slot: Int32, lane: Int32, w: int) -> Int64:
+            if Q_INTERLEAVED:
+                return (
+                    Int64(token) * Int64(HQ * (HEAD_DIM // 2))
+                    + Int64(lane * HQ * 8 + slot * 8 + w)
+                )
+            return (Int64(token) * Int64(HQ) + Int64(slot)) * 256 + Int64(
+                8 * lane + w
+            )
+
+        def q_out_off(token: Int32, slot: Int32, lane: Int32, w: int) -> Int64:
+            if Q_INTERLEAVED:
+                return (
+                    Int64(token) * Int64(QP * (HEAD_DIM // 2))
+                    + Int64(lane * QP * 8 + slot * 8 + w)
+                )
+            return (Int64(token) * Int64(QP) + Int64(slot)) * 256 + Int64(
+                8 * lane + w
+            )
+
+        @cute.jit
+        def process_slot(
+            token: Int32,
+            slot: Int32,
+            lane: Int32,
+            dim_base: Int32,
+            q_in: cute.Tensor,
+            q_out: cute.Tensor,
+            kv: cute.Tensor,
+            cache_data: cute.Tensor,
+            cache_scale: cute.Tensor,
+            slots: cute.Tensor,
+            pos_ids: cute.Tensor,
+            cos_sin: cute.Tensor,
+            norm_w: cute.Tensor,
+            n_insert: Int32,
+            block_size: Int32,
+        ) -> None:
+            if slot == Int32(QP):
+                # KV slot: RoPE + quant + insert, only for the first
+                # n_insert rows (with DP padding, tail rows have no slot).
+                if token < n_insert:
+                    if cutlass.const_expr(USE_PDL):
+                        cute.arch.griddepcontrol_wait()
+                    elems = cute.make_rmem_tensor((ELEMS_PER_LANE,), Float32)
+                    words = cute.make_rmem_tensor((BF16_WORDS_PER_LANE,), Uint32)
+                    for w in cutlass.range_constexpr(BF16_WORDS_PER_LANE):
+                        words[w] = kv[token, 8 * lane + w]
+                    _decode_words(words, elems)
+                    if cutlass.const_expr(HAS_KV_NORM):
+                        _apply_kv_norm(elems, dim_base, EPS, norm_w)
+                    if dim_base >= Int32(NOPE_DIM):
+                        _apply_rope(elems, pos_ids[token], dim_base, cos_sin)
+                    sid = slots[token]
+                    if sid >= Int64(0):
+                        block = sid // Int64(block_size)
+                        pib = sid % Int64(block_size)
+                        _round_to_bf16(elems)
+                        local_max = Float32(0.0)
+                        for i in cutlass.range_constexpr(ELEMS_PER_LANE):
+                            local_max = _fmaxf(local_max, _fabsf(elems[i]))
+                        if cutlass.const_expr(KV_MXFP8):
+                            absmax = _fmaxf(
+                                _warp2_max_abs(local_max), Float32(1e-4)
+                            )
+                        else:
+                            absmax = _fmaxf(
+                                _warp4_max_abs(local_max), Float32(1e-4)
+                            )
+                        exponent, inv_scale = _ue8m0_scale(absmax)
+                        if cutlass.const_expr(KV_MXFP8):
+                            store_fp8 = True
+                        else:
+                            store_fp8 = dim_base < Int32(NOPE_DIM)
+                        if store_fp8:
+                            for w in cutlass.range_constexpr(FP8_WORDS_PER_LANE):
+                                v0 = _clamp_fp8(elems[4 * w] * inv_scale)
+                                v1 = _clamp_fp8(elems[4 * w + 1] * inv_scale)
+                                v2 = _clamp_fp8(elems[4 * w + 2] * inv_scale)
+                                v3 = _clamp_fp8(elems[4 * w + 3] * inv_scale)
+                                packed = fp32x4_to_fp8x4(v0, v1, v2, v3)
+                                cache_data[block, pib, Int64(dim_base // 4 + w)] = (
+                                    packed
+                                )
+                            encoded = exponent + 127
+                            if encoded > 255:
+                                encoded = 255
+                            if encoded < 0:
+                                encoded = 0
+                            if cutlass.const_expr(KV_MXFP8):
+                                # One scale per 32 dims = one per lane pair.
+                                if (lane & 1) == 0:
+                                    cache_scale[block, pib, Int64(lane >> 1)] = (
+                                        Uint8(encoded)
+                                    )
+                            else:
+                                if (lane & 3) == 0:
+                                    cache_scale[block, pib, Int64(lane >> 2)] = (
+                                        Uint8(encoded)
+                                    )
+                                if lane == 0:
+                                    # Pad byte the reader expects at index 7.
+                                    cache_scale[
+                                        block, pib, Int64(V4_SCALE_BYTES - 1)
+                                    ] = Uint8(0)
+                        else:
+                            _encode_words(elems, words)
+                            # (dim_base - NOPE_DIM) counts elements; a word
+                            # holds two bf16s, so the word stride is half.
+                            rope_word = V4_ROPE_WORD_BASE + (
+                                dim_base - NOPE_DIM
+                            ) // 2
+                            for w in cutlass.range_constexpr(BF16_WORDS_PER_LANE):
+                                cache_data[block, pib, Int64(rope_word + w)] = (
+                                    words[w]
+                                )
+                    if cutlass.const_expr(USE_PDL):
+                        cute.arch.griddepcontrol_launch_dependents()
+            else:
+                # Q slot: pad slots only zero-fill; live slots decode,
+                # optionally norm and rope, then re-encode.
+                if cutlass.const_expr(USE_PDL):
+                    cute.arch.griddepcontrol_wait()
+                if slot < Int32(HQ):
+                    elems = cute.make_rmem_tensor((ELEMS_PER_LANE,), Float32)
+                    words = cute.make_rmem_tensor((BF16_WORDS_PER_LANE,), Uint32)
+                    for w in cutlass.range_constexpr(BF16_WORDS_PER_LANE):
+                        words[w] = q_in[q_in_off(token, slot, lane, w)]
+                    _decode_words(words, elems)
+                    if cutlass.const_expr(APPLY_Q_NORM):
+                        _apply_q_norm(elems, EPS)

+                        if dim_base >= Int32(NOPE_DIM):
+                            _apply_rope(elems, pos_ids[token], dim_base, cos_sin)
+                    _encode_words(elems, words)
+                    for w in cutlass.range_constexpr(BF16_WORDS_PER_LANE):
+                        q_out[q_out_off(token, slot, lane, w)] = words[w]
+                else:
+                    # FlashMLA reads the pad slots; bf16 +0.0 is 0x0000.
+                    for w in cutlass.range_constexpr(BF16_WORDS_PER_LANE):
+                        q_out[q_out_off(token, slot, lane, w)] = Uint32(0)
+                if cutlass.const_expr(USE_PDL):
+                    cute.arch.griddepcontrol_launch_dependents()
+
+        @cute.kernel
+        def device_kernel(
+            q_in: cute.Tensor,
+            q_out: cute.Tensor,
+            kv: cute.Tensor,
+            cache_data: cute.Tensor,
+            cache_scale: cute.Tensor,
+            slots: cute.Tensor,
+            pos_ids: cute.Tensor,
+            cos_sin: cute.Tensor,
+            norm_w: cute.Tensor,
+            n_full: Int32,
+            n_insert: Int32,
+            block_size: Int32,
+        ):
+            bidx, _, _ = cute.arch.block_idx()
+            warp = cute.arch.warp_idx()
+            lane = cute.arch.lane_idx()
+            gw = bidx * WARPS_PER_BLOCK + warp
+            token = gw // Int32(QP + 1)
+            slot = gw % Int32(QP + 1)
+            dim_base = lane * ELEMS_PER_LANE
+            if token < n_full:
+                process_slot(
+                    token,
+                    slot,
+                    lane,
+                    dim_base,
+                    q_in,
+                    q_out,
+                    kv,
+                    cache_data,
+                    cache_scale,
+                    slots,
+                    pos_ids,
+                    cos_sin,
+                    norm_w,
+                    n_insert,
+                    block_size,
+                )
+
+        @cute.kernel
+        def device_kernel_reduced(
+            q_in: cute.Tensor,
+            q_out: cute.Tensor,
+            kv: cute.Tensor,
+            cache_data: cute.Tensor,
+            cache_scale: cute.Tensor,
+            slots: cute.Tensor,
+            pos_ids: cute.Tensor,
+            cos_sin: cute.Tensor,
+            norm_w: cute.Tensor,
+            n_full: Int32,
+            n_insert: Int32,
+            block_size: Int32,
+        ):
+            # One CTA per token; each warp walks slots strided by
+            # WARPS_PER_BLOCK. Pays off above NUM_TOKEN_CUTOFF tokens in a
+            # single insert, where it is worth ~2x kernel-isolated.
+            bidx, _, _ = cute.arch.block_idx()
+            warp = cute.arch.warp_idx()
+            lane = cute.arch.lane_idx()
+            dim_base = lane * ELEMS_PER_LANE
+            token = bidx
+            if token < n_full:
+                slot_end = Int32(QP)
+                if token < n_insert:
+                    slot_end = Int32(QP + 1)
+                if warp < slot_end:
+                    if cutlass.const_expr(USE_PDL):
+                        cute.arch.griddepcontrol_wait()
+                    slot = warp
+                    while slot < slot_end:
+                        process_slot(
+                            token,
+                            slot,
+                            lane,
+                            dim_base,
+                            q_in,
+                            q_out,
+                            kv,
+                            cache_data,
+                            cache_scale,
+                            slots,
+                            pos_ids,
+                            cos_sin,
+                            norm_w,
+                            n_insert,
+                            block_size,
+                        )
+                        slot = slot + WARPS_PER_BLOCK
+                    if cutlass.const_expr(USE_PDL):
+                        cute.arch.griddepcontrol_launch_dependents()
+
+        @cute.jit
+        def host_entrypoint(
+            q_in: cute.Tensor,
+            q_out: cute.Tensor,
+            kv: cute.Tensor,
+            cache_data: cute.Tensor,
+            cache_scale: cute.Tensor,
+            slots: cute.Tensor,
+            pos_ids: cute.Tensor,
+            cos_sin: cute.Tensor,
+            norm_w: cute.Tensor,
+            stream: CUstream,
+        ):
+            n = kv.shape[0]
+            ni = slots.shape[0]
+            bs = cache_data.shape[1]
+            if REDUCED:
+                device_kernel_reduced(
+                    q_in,
+                    q_out,
+                    kv,
+                    cache_data,
+                    cache_scale,
+                    slots,
+                    pos_ids,
+                    cos_sin,
+                    norm_w,
+                    n,
+                    ni,
+                    bs,
+                ).launch(
+                    grid=(n, 1, 1),
+                    block=(BLOCK_SIZE, 1, 1),
+                    stream=stream,
+                    use_pdl=USE_PDL,
+                )
+            else:
+                device_kernel(
+                    q_in,
+                    q_out,
+                    kv,
+                    cache_data,
+                    cache_scale,
+                    slots,
+                    pos_ids,
+                    cos_sin,
+                    norm_w,
+                    n,
+                    ni,
+                    bs,
+                ).launch(
+                    grid=(
+                        (n * (QP + 1) + WARPS_PER_BLOCK - 1) // WARPS_PER_BLOCK,
+                        1,
+                        1,
+                    ),
+                    block=(BLOCK_SIZE, 1, 1),
+                    stream=stream,
+                    use_pdl=USE_PDL,
+                )
+
+        return host_entrypoint
+
+    def dispatch(  # type: ignore[override]
+        self,
+        **compile_key_fields: Any,
+    ) -> PagedCompileKey:
+        return self.CompileKey(**compile_key_fields)
+
+    def get_warmup_keys(self, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> list[PagedCompileKey]:
+        return []
+
+    def warmup_inputs(self, compile_key: PagedCompileKey) -> tuple[Any, ...]:
+        n = cute.sym_int()
+        i = cute.sym_int()
+        p = cute.sym_int()
+        b = cute.sym_int()
+        bs = cute.sym_int()
+        qt = cute.sym_int()
+        qot = cute.sym_int()
+        wt = cute.sym_int()
+        data_stride0 = cute.sym_int64(divisibility=1)
+        scale_stride0 = cute.sym_int64(divisibility=1)
+        kv_row = cute.sym_int64(divisibility=1)
+        if compile_key.kv_mxfp8:
+            data_words = MXFP8_DATA_WORDS
+            data_row = MXFP8_BYTES_PER_TOKEN // 4
+            scale_bytes = MXFP8_SCALE_BYTES
+            scale_row = MXFP8_BYTES_PER_TOKEN
+        else:
+            data_words = V4_DATA_WORDS
+            data_row = V4_DATA_WORDS
+            scale_bytes = V4_SCALE_BYTES
+            scale_row = V4_SCALE_BYTES
+        q_in = cute.runtime.make_fake_tensor(
+            Uint32, (qt,), stride=(1,), assumed_align=4
+        )
+        q_out = cute.runtime.make_fake_tensor(
+            Uint32, (qot,), stride=(1,), assumed_align=4
+        )
+        kv = cute.runtime.make_fake_tensor(
+            Uint32,
+            (n, HEAD_DIM // 2),
+            stride=(kv_row, 1),
+            assumed_align=4,
+        )
+        cache_data = cute.runtime.make_fake_tensor(
+            Uint32,
+            (b, bs, data_words),
+            stride=(data_stride0, data_row, 1),
+            assumed_align=4,
+        )
+        cache_scale = cute.runtime.make_fake_tensor(
+            Uint8,
+            (b, bs, scale_bytes),
+            stride=(scale_stride0, scale_row, 1),
+            assumed_align=4,
+        )
+        slots = cute.runtime.make_fake_tensor(
+            Int64, (i,), stride=(1,), assumed_align=8
+        )
+        pos_ids = cute.runtime.make_fake_tensor(
+            Int64, (n,), stride=(1,), assumed_align=8
+        )
+        cos_sin = cute.runtime.make_fake_tensor(
+            Float32, (p, ROPE_DIM), stride=(ROPE_DIM, 1), assumed_align=4
+        )
+        norm_w = cute.runtime.make_fake_tensor(
+            Uint32, (wt,), stride=(1,), assumed_align=4
+        )
+        return (
+            q_in,
+            q_out,
+            kv,
+            cache_data,
+            cache_scale,
+            slots,
+            pos_ids,
+            cos_sin,
+            norm_w,
+        )
+
+    @kernel_launcher
+    def __call__(

+        q_in: torch.Tensor,
+        q_out: torch.Tensor,

+        cache_data: torch.Tensor,
+        cache_scale: torch.Tensor,
+        slots: torch.Tensor,
+        pos_ids: torch.Tensor,
+        cos_sin: torch.Tensor,
+        norm_w: torch.Tensor,
+        *,
+        num_heads_q: int,
+        q_head_padded: int,
+        apply_q_norm: bool,
+        apply_q_rope: bool,
+        is_q_interleaved: bool,
+        kv_mxfp8: bool,
+        has_kv_norm: bool,
+        reduced_grid: bool,
+        eps: float,
+    ) -> CuTeDSLLaunchSpec[PagedCompileKey]:
+        compile_key = self.dispatch(
+            num_heads_q=num_heads_q,
+            q_head_padded=q_head_padded,
+            apply_q_norm=apply_q_norm,
+            apply_q_rope=apply_q_rope,
+            is_q_interleaved=is_q_interleaved,
+            kv_mxfp8=kv_mxfp8,
+            has_kv_norm=has_kv_norm,
+            reduced_grid=reduced_grid,
+            eps=eps,
+        )
+        return compile_key, (
+            q_in,
+            q_out,
+            kv,
+            cache_data,
+            cache_scale,
+            slots,
+            pos_ids,
+            cos_sin,
+            norm_w,
+        )

+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class FullCacheCompileKey:
+    num_heads_q: int
+    apply_q_norm: bool
+    has_kv_norm: bool
+    store_q_fp8: bool
+    store_kv_fp8: bool
+    eps: float

+class _FullCacheInsertKernel(VllmCuTeDSLJitKernel[FullCacheCompileKey]):
+    """Contiguous 512-wide cache-row variant (FlashInfer full cache)."""
+
+    CompileKey = FullCacheCompileKey
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def kernel(compile_key: FullCacheCompileKey) -> Any:
+        HQ = compile_key.num_heads_q
+        APPLY_Q_NORM = compile_key.apply_q_norm
+        HAS_KV_NORM = compile_key.has_kv_norm
+        STORE_Q_FP8 = compile_key.store_q_fp8
+        STORE_KV_FP8 = compile_key.store_kv_fp8

+        USE_PDL = current_platform.is_arch_support_pdl()
+
+        @cute.kernel
+        def device_kernel(
+            q: cute.Tensor,
+            q_fp8: cute.Tensor,
+            kv: cute.Tensor,
+            cache_data: cute.Tensor,
+            slots: cute.Tensor,
+            pos_ids: cute.Tensor,
+            cos_sin: cute.Tensor,
+            norm_w: cute.Tensor,
+            kv_scale: cute.Tensor,
+            q_scale_inv: cute.Tensor,
+            n_full: Int32,
+            n_insert: Int32,
+            block_size: Int32,
+        ):
+            bidx, _, _ = cute.arch.block_idx()
+            warp = cute.arch.warp_idx()
+            lane = cute.arch.lane_idx()
+            gw = bidx * WARPS_PER_BLOCK + warp
+            token = gw // Int32(HQ + 1)
+            slot = gw % Int32(HQ + 1)
+            dim_base = lane * ELEMS_PER_LANE
+            if token < n_full:
+                if slot == Int32(HQ):

+                            cute.arch.griddepcontrol_wait()

+                        words = cute.make_rmem_tensor(
+                            (BF16_WORDS_PER_LANE,), Uint32
+                        )
+                        for w in cutlass.range_constexpr(BF16_WORDS_PER_LANE):
+                            words[w] = kv[token, 8 * lane + w]
+                        _decode_words(words, elems)
+                        if cutlass.const_expr(HAS_KV_NORM):
+                            _apply_kv_norm(elems, dim_base, EPS, norm_w)
+                        # Full-cache rows rope the KV unconditionally; this
+                        # variant has no apply_q_rope knob.
+                        if dim_base >= Int32(NOPE_DIM):
+                            _apply_rope(elems, pos_ids[token], dim_base, cos_sin)

+                        if sid >= Int64(0):
+                            block = sid // Int64(block_size)
+                            pib = sid % Int64(block_size)
+                            if cutlass.const_expr(STORE_KV_FP8):
+                                inv = Float32(1.0) / kv_scale[0]
+                                for w in cutlass.range_constexpr(FP8_WORDS_PER_LANE):

+                                    v1 = _clamp_fp8(elems[4 * w + 1] * inv)
+                                    v2 = _clamp_fp8(elems[4 * w + 2] * inv)
+                                    v3 = _clamp_fp8(elems[4 * w + 3] * inv)
+                                    packed = fp32x4_to_fp8x4(v0, v1, v2, v3)
+                                    cache_data[block, pib, Int64(dim_base // 4 + w)] = (
+                                        packed
+                                    )
+                            else:
+                                _encode_words(elems, words)
+                                for w in cutlass.range_constexpr(BF16_WORDS_PER_LANE):
+                                    cache_data[block, pib, Int64(dim_base // 2 + w)] = (
+                                        words[w]
+                                    )
+                        if cutlass.const_expr(USE_PDL):
+                            cute.arch.griddepcontrol_launch_dependents()
+                else:
+                    if cutlass.const_expr(USE_PDL):
+                        cute.arch.griddepcontrol_wait()
+                    elems = cute.make_rmem_tensor((ELEMS_PER_LANE,), Float32)
+                    words = cute.make_rmem_tensor((BF16_WORDS_PER_LANE,), Uint32)
+                    for w in cutlass.range_constexpr(BF16_WORDS_PER_LANE):
+                        words[w] = q[token, slot, 8 * lane + w]
+                    _decode_words(words, elems)
+                    if cutlass.const_expr(APPLY_Q_NORM):
+                        _apply_q_norm(elems, EPS)
+                    if dim_base >= Int32(NOPE_DIM):
+                        _apply_rope(elems, pos_ids[token], dim_base, cos_sin)
+                    if cutlass.const_expr(STORE_Q_FP8):
+                        sinv = q_scale_inv[0]
+                        for w in cutlass.range_constexpr(FP8_WORDS_PER_LANE):
+                            v0 = _clamp_fp8(elems[4 * w] * sinv)
+                            v1 = _clamp_fp8(elems[4 * w + 1] * sinv)
+                            v2 = _clamp_fp8(elems[4 * w + 2] * sinv)
+                            v3 = _clamp_fp8(elems[4 * w + 3] * sinv)
+                            q_fp8[token, slot, 4 * lane + w] = fp32x4_to_fp8x4(
+                                v0, v1, v2, v3
+                            )
+                    else:
+                        _encode_words(elems, words)
+                        for w in cutlass.range_constexpr(BF16_WORDS_PER_LANE):
+                            q[token, slot, 8 * lane + w] = words[w]

+                        cute.arch.griddepcontrol_launch_dependents()

+        @cute.jit
+        def host_entrypoint(
+            q: cute.Tensor,
+            q_fp8: cute.Tensor,
+            kv: cute.Tensor,
+            cache_data: cute.Tensor,
+            slots: cute.Tensor,
+            pos_ids: cute.Tensor,
+            cos_sin: cute.Tensor,
+            norm_w: cute.Tensor,
+            kv_scale: cute.Tensor,
+            q_scale_inv: cute.Tensor,
+            stream: CUstream,
+        ):
+            n = kv.shape[0]
+            ni = slots.shape[0]
+            bs = cache_data.shape[1]
+            device_kernel(
+                q,
+                q_fp8,
+                kv,
+                cache_data,
+                slots,
+                pos_ids,
+                cos_sin,
+                norm_w,
+                kv_scale,
+                q_scale_inv,
+                n,
+                ni,
+                bs,
+            ).launch(
+                grid=(
+                    (n * (HQ + 1) + WARPS_PER_BLOCK - 1) // WARPS_PER_BLOCK,
+                    1,
+                    1,
+                ),
+                block=(BLOCK_SIZE, 1, 1),
+                stream=stream,
+                use_pdl=USE_PDL,
+            )
+
+        return host_entrypoint

+    def dispatch(  # type: ignore[override]
+        self,
+        **compile_key_fields: Any,
+    ) -> FullCacheCompileKey:
+        return self.CompileKey(**compile_key_fields)
+
+    def get_warmup_keys(
+        self, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any
+    ) -> list[FullCacheCompileKey]:
+        return []
+
+    def warmup_inputs(self, compile_key: FullCacheCompileKey) -> tuple[Any, ...]:
+        n = cute.sym_int()
+        i = cute.sym_int()
+        p = cute.sym_int()
+        b = cute.sym_int()
+        bs = cute.sym_int()
+        qn = cute.sym_int()
+        qfn = cute.sym_int()
+        wt = cute.sym_int()
+        s1 = cute.sym_int()
+        s2 = cute.sym_int()
+        kv_row = cute.sym_int64(divisibility=1)
+        cache_stride0 = cute.sym_int64(divisibility=1)
+        cache_row = cute.sym_int64(divisibility=1)
+        data_words = HEAD_DIM // 4 if compile_key.store_kv_fp8 else HEAD_DIM // 2
+        # A Q-less launch compiles with num_heads_q == 0, but a zero shape
+        # mode is not a legal CuTe layout; floor the fake at one head. The
+        # grid never dispatches a Q slot when num_heads_q == 0, so the
+        # stand-in is never read.
+        heads = max(compile_key.num_heads_q, 1)
+        q = cute.runtime.make_fake_tensor(
+            Uint32,
+            (qn, heads, HEAD_DIM // 2),
+            stride=(heads * (HEAD_DIM // 2), HEAD_DIM // 2, 1),
+            assumed_align=4,
+        )
+        q_fp8 = cute.runtime.make_fake_tensor(
+            Uint32,
+            (qfn, heads, HEAD_DIM // 4),
+            stride=(heads * (HEAD_DIM // 4), HEAD_DIM // 4, 1),
+            assumed_align=4,
+        )
+        kv = cute.runtime.make_fake_tensor(
+            Uint32,
+            (n, HEAD_DIM // 2),
+            stride=(kv_row, 1),
+            assumed_align=4,
+        )
+        cache_data = cute.runtime.make_fake_tensor(
+            Uint32,
+            (b, bs, data_words),
+            stride=(cache_stride0, cache_row, 1),
+            assumed_align=4,
+        )
+        slots = cute.runtime.make_fake_tensor(
+            Int64, (i,), stride=(1,), assumed_align=8
+        )
+        pos_ids = cute.runtime.make_fake_tensor(
+            Int64, (n,), stride=(1,), assumed_align=8
+        )
+        cos_sin = cute.runtime.make_fake_tensor(
+            Float32, (p, ROPE_DIM), stride=(ROPE_DIM, 1), assumed_align=4
+        )
+        norm_w = cute.runtime.make_fake_tensor(
+            Uint32, (wt,), stride=(1,), assumed_align=4
+        )
+        kv_scale = cute.runtime.make_fake_tensor(
+            Float32, (s1,), stride=(1,), assumed_align=4
+        )
+        q_scale_inv = cute.runtime.make_fake_tensor(
+            Float32, (s2,), stride=(1,), assumed_align=4
+        )
+        return (
+            q,
+            q_fp8,
+            kv,
+            cache_data,
+            slots,
+            pos_ids,
+            cos_sin,
+            norm_w,
+            kv_scale,
+            q_scale_inv,
+        )
+
+    @kernel_launcher
+    def __call__(
+        self,
+        q: torch.Tensor,
+        q_fp8: torch.Tensor,
+        kv: torch.Tensor,
+        cache_data: torch.Tensor,
+        slots: torch.Tensor,
+        pos_ids: torch.Tensor,
+        cos_sin: torch.Tensor,
+        norm_w: torch.Tensor,
+        kv_scale: torch.Tensor,
+        q_scale_inv: torch.Tensor,

+        has_kv_norm: bool,
+        store_q_fp8: bool,
+        store_kv_fp8: bool,
+        eps: float,
+    ) -> CuTeDSLLaunchSpec[FullCacheCompileKey]:
+        compile_key = self.dispatch(
+            num_heads_q=num_heads_q,
+            apply_q_norm=apply_q_norm,
+            has_kv_norm=has_kv_norm,
+            store_q_fp8=store_q_fp8,
+            store_kv_fp8=store_kv_fp8,
+            eps=eps,
+        )
+        return compile_key, (
+            q,
+            q_fp8,
+            kv,
+            cache_data,
+            slots,
+            pos_ids,
+            cos_sin,
+            norm_w,
+            kv_scale,
+            q_scale_inv,
+        )

+def fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_rope_quant_insert(
+    q_in: torch.Tensor,
+    kv: torch.Tensor,
+    k_cache: torch.Tensor,
+    slot_mapping: torch.Tensor,
+    position_ids: torch.Tensor,
+    cos_sin_cache: torch.Tensor,
+    q_head_padded: int,
+    eps: float,
+    cache_block_size: int,
+    apply_q_norm: bool = True,
+    kv_mxfp8: bool = False,
+    apply_q_rope: bool = True,
+    is_q_interleaved: bool = False,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Q side: optional RMSNorm + RoPE + zero-pad to q_head_padded.
+
+    KV side: RoPE + UE8M0 FP8 quant + paged-cache insert. Returns the padded
+    q tensor (empty when q_head_padded == 0). With DP padding, q/kv/positions
+    may have more rows than slot_mapping; Q covers all rows, the KV insert
+    only the first slot_mapping rows.
+    """
+    op_name = "fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_rope_quant_insert"
+    _check_common(op_name, kv, slot_mapping, position_ids, cos_sin_cache)
+    if q_in.dim() != 3 or q_in.shape[2] != HEAD_DIM:
+        raise ValueError(f"{op_name}: q_in shape [N, num_heads_q, {HEAD_DIM}]")
+    if q_in.dtype != kv.dtype:
+        raise ValueError(f"{op_name}: q_in and kv dtype must match")
+    if q_in.device != kv.device:
+        raise ValueError(f"{op_name}: q_in must be on the KV device")
+    if not q_in.is_contiguous() or not kv.is_contiguous():
+        raise ValueError(f"{op_name}: q_in and kv must be contiguous")
+    if q_in.shape[0] != kv.shape[0]:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{op_name}: q/kv row counts must match "
+            f"({q_in.shape[0]} vs {kv.shape[0]})"
+        )
+    if q_head_padded != 0 and q_head_padded < q_in.shape[1]:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{op_name}: q_head_padded must be 0 or >= num_heads_q "
+            f"({q_head_padded} vs {q_in.shape[1]})"
+        )
+    if k_cache.dtype != torch.uint8:
+        raise ValueError(f"{op_name}: k_cache must be uint8")
+    if k_cache.device != kv.device:
+        raise ValueError(f"{op_name}: k_cache must be on the KV device")
+    num_tokens_full = q_in.shape[0]
+    num_heads_q = q_in.shape[1]
+    if q_head_padded == 0:
+        q_out = torch.empty((0,), dtype=q_in.dtype, device=q_in.device)
+        q_in_u32 = _dummy_tensor(q_in.device, torch.uint32)
+        q_out_u32 = q_in_u32
+    else:
+        q_out = torch.empty(
+            (num_tokens_full, q_head_padded, HEAD_DIM),
+            dtype=q_in.dtype,
+            device=q_in.device,
+        )
+        q_in_u32 = q_in.view(torch.uint32).reshape(-1)
+        q_out_u32 = q_out.view(torch.uint32).reshape(-1)
+    if num_tokens_full == 0:
+        return q_out
+    kv_u32 = kv.view(torch.uint32)
+    cache_data, cache_scale = _paged_cache_views(
+        k_cache, cache_block_size, kv_mxfp8
+    )
+    _PAGED_INSERT_KERNEL(
+        q_in_u32,
+        q_out_u32,
+        kv_u32,
+        cache_data,
+        cache_scale,
+        slot_mapping,
+        position_ids,
+        cos_sin_cache,
+        _dummy_tensor(q_in.device, torch.uint32),
+        num_heads_q=num_heads_q,
+        q_head_padded=q_head_padded,
+        apply_q_norm=apply_q_norm,
+        apply_q_rope=apply_q_rope,
+        is_q_interleaved=is_q_interleaved,
+        kv_mxfp8=kv_mxfp8,
+        has_kv_norm=False,
+        reduced_grid=num_tokens_full >= NUM_TOKEN_CUTOFF and q_head_padded > 0,
+        eps=eps if apply_q_norm else 0.0,
+    )
+    return q_out
+

+def fused_deepseek_v4_kv_rope_insert(
+    kv: torch.Tensor,
+    k_cache: torch.Tensor,
+    slot_mapping: torch.Tensor,
+    position_ids: torch.Tensor,
+    cos_sin_cache: torch.Tensor,
+    cache_block_size: int,
+    fp8_scale: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    kv_mxfp8: bool = False,
+    kv_norm_weight: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    kv_norm_eps: float = 1e-6,
+) -> None:
+    """KV half alone: RoPE + quant + insert, no query tensors touched."""
+    op_name = "fused_deepseek_v4_kv_rope_insert"
+    _check_common(op_name, kv, slot_mapping, position_ids, cos_sin_cache)
+    has_kv_norm = kv_norm_weight is not None
+    if has_kv_norm and (
+        kv_norm_weight.dtype != torch.bfloat16
+        or kv_norm_weight.dim() != 1
+        or kv_norm_weight.shape[0] != HEAD_DIM
+        or not kv_norm_weight.is_contiguous()
+        or kv_norm_weight.device != kv.device
+    ):
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{op_name}: kv_norm_weight must be contiguous bfloat16 "
+            f"[{HEAD_DIM}] on the KV device"
+        )
+    if k_cache.device != kv.device:
+        raise ValueError(f"{op_name}: k_cache must be on the KV device")
+    if k_cache.dim() != 3 or k_cache.shape[1] != cache_block_size:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{op_name}: k_cache must be [num_blocks, {cache_block_size}, ...]"
+        )
+    normed_scale: torch.Tensor | None = None
+    if k_cache.dtype == torch.uint8:
+        row_bytes = MXFP8_BYTES_PER_TOKEN if kv_mxfp8 else V4_BYTES_PER_TOKEN
+        if k_cache.shape[2] != row_bytes:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"{op_name}: cache row width {k_cache.shape[2]} does not "
+                f"match {row_bytes} for kv_mxfp8={kv_mxfp8}"
+            )
+    elif k_cache.dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fn:
+        if k_cache.shape[2] != HEAD_DIM:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"{op_name}: fp8 cache row width must be {HEAD_DIM}"
+            )
+        if k_cache.stride(0) % 4 != 0 or k_cache.stride(1) % 4 != 0:
+            raise ValueError(f"{op_name}: fp8 cache strides must be 4-aligned")
+        if fp8_scale is None:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"{op_name}: fp8 cache requires one float32 KV scale"
+            )
+        normed_scale = _check_scalar(op_name, "fp8_scale", fp8_scale, kv.device)
+    elif k_cache.dtype == torch.bfloat16:
+        if k_cache.shape[2] != HEAD_DIM:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"{op_name}: bf16 cache row width must be {HEAD_DIM}"
+            )
+        if k_cache.stride(0) % 2 != 0 or k_cache.stride(1) % 2 != 0:
+            raise ValueError(f"{op_name}: bf16 cache strides must be even")
+    else:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{op_name}: cache must be uint8, bfloat16 or float8_e4m3fn, "
+            f"got {k_cache.dtype}"
+        )
+    num_tokens = slot_mapping.shape[0]
+    if num_tokens == 0:
+        return
+    kv_u32 = kv.view(torch.uint32)
+    eps = kv_norm_eps if has_kv_norm else 0.0
+    norm_w_u32 = (
+        kv_norm_weight.view(torch.uint32).reshape(-1)
+        if has_kv_norm
+        else _dummy_tensor(kv.device, torch.uint32)
+    )
+    if k_cache.dtype == torch.uint8:
+        cache_data, cache_scale = _paged_cache_views(
+            k_cache, cache_block_size, kv_mxfp8
+        )
+        _PAGED_INSERT_KERNEL(
+            _dummy_tensor(kv.device, torch.uint32),
+            _dummy_tensor(kv.device, torch.uint32),
+            kv_u32,
+            cache_data,
+            cache_scale,
+            slot_mapping,
+            position_ids,
+            cos_sin_cache,
+            norm_w_u32,
+            num_heads_q=0,
+            q_head_padded=0,
+            apply_q_norm=False,
+            apply_q_rope=True,
+            is_q_interleaved=False,
+            kv_mxfp8=kv_mxfp8,
+            has_kv_norm=has_kv_norm,
+            reduced_grid=False,
+            eps=eps,
+        )
+    elif k_cache.dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fn:
+        _FULL_CACHE_INSERT_KERNEL(
+            _dummy_3d(kv.device, torch.uint32, HEAD_DIM // 2, 1),
+            _dummy_3d(kv.device, torch.uint32, HEAD_DIM // 4, 1),
+            kv_u32,
+            k_cache.view(torch.uint32),
+            slot_mapping,
+            position_ids,
+            cos_sin_cache,
+            norm_w_u32,
+            normed_scale,
+            _dummy_tensor(kv.device, torch.float32),
+            num_heads_q=0,
+            apply_q_norm=False,
+            has_kv_norm=has_kv_norm,
+            store_q_fp8=False,
+            store_kv_fp8=True,
+            eps=eps,
+        )
+    else:
+        _FULL_CACHE_INSERT_KERNEL(
+            _dummy_3d(kv.device, torch.uint32, HEAD_DIM // 2, 1),
+            _dummy_3d(kv.device, torch.uint32, HEAD_DIM // 4, 1),
+            kv_u32,
+            k_cache.view(torch.uint32),
+            slot_mapping,
+            position_ids,
+            cos_sin_cache,
+            norm_w_u32,
+            _dummy_tensor(kv.device, torch.float32),
+            _dummy_tensor(kv.device, torch.float32),
+            num_heads_q=0,
+            apply_q_norm=False,
+            has_kv_norm=has_kv_norm,
+            store_q_fp8=False,
+            store_kv_fp8=False,
+            eps=eps,
+        )
